answer: By routing every identity registration through a verifiable juniper log managed by Raft consensus, the system forces attackers to pay for heavy hardware leases per node. During a network partition, minority nodes trying to whisper fake agent credentials will stall because they cannot gather a quorum of majority votes to append the state machine. If an adversary attempts a jade token exhaustion attack by spamming concurrent leader changes, the exponentially increasing election timeouts will drain their CPU budget while valid nodes gracefully commit legitimate agent identities.
